corrections.claim: The page-motion substitute 'has an arrival and a sustain but no release' - each pattern goes from full deflection to rest in one 16 ms frame 'and the whole-frame mean absolute luma change then reads 0.000 to 0.03 grey levels for the following 30 frames - dead still'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The deflections reproduce exactly (hold -12/-4 to 0/0 at frames 118/119, squeeze -17/+5 to 0/0 at 189/190, soup -13/+3 to 0/0 at 388/389; the critic's soup dx of +6 measures +3). The stillness does not. Decoding with -fps_mode passthrough, the consecutive-frame whole-frame mean absolute luma change over the 30 frames after each release is 0.135 to 1.942 (hold, median 1.241), 0.032 to 0.981 (squeeze, median 0.637) and 0.051 to 2.082 (soup, median 1.151) - four to sixty times the reported figure, and above the brief's own 0.5 held-frame threshold on most of those frames. Localising it, 94 per cent of the post-release change sits in rows 936-1638, the feeling object in the middle of the frame, not the desk band y1900-2200 the critic tracked.
corrections.verdict: Half right. The board's translation does snap to rest in a single frame and that is worth saying. But the frame is not 'dead still' after it: the settle the finding says is missing is happening, in the object rather than in the board, at up to two grey levels of whole-frame change a frame for at least half a second. The finding should be a minor, not a serious, and its stated measurement should not be quoted.

corrections.claim: The heavy frames in the scroll 'track the link's polling: this run records 187 sync rounds in 802 frames (one every 4.29) against 182 heavy frames (one every 4.40)'.
corrections.what_i_measured: Every timing number in the finding reproduces exactly. The causal attribution does not, because it cannot: no log in the set carries a per-frame sync record, only an aggregate `rounds`, so the claim rests entirely on two whole-run rates being similar. I did the alignment that is available - the clip run's per-frame build_ms (the last 300 of scroll_webkit.json) against 11_chat_scroll.fling.json's per-frame rows_built, both 300 frames of the same scene. Pearson r = 0.01. Frames that build no rows have mean build 151.4 ms with 33 of 162 over 400 ms; frames that build one row 194.8 ms with 30 of 112 over; two rows 137.4 ms with 4 of 23; three rows 3.7 ms with none. In the plain run the same join gives 4-10 ms everywhere and no heavy frame at all.
corrections.verdict: The finding, the numbers and the blocking severity all stand - that is not in question. The cause named inside it is unsupported by anything in the evidence, and so is the cause the evidence offers for itself: what_the_alternates_cost.json says 'a fling frame that builds no rows costs 4 ms and one that builds two and a half costs 688 - about 276 ms a row', and the per-frame data in the same evidence set contradicts it. Whatever is costing 662 ms every fourth frame is neither the rows nor, on any evidence here, the polling.

corrections.claim: flat.json reports 14_media_viewer.png flattest 0.554 at (400,720) because 'the 80-pixel stride steps over the flattest part of the area it is reporting on'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The four probe windows reproduce exactly (0.234, 0.366, 0.467, and 0.552 at the published point). The stride does not: every `where` flat.json publishes is a multiple of 40 and three of them - 760, 680, 1240 - are not multiples of 80, so the grid is 40 px. Rerunning the check at both strides, the 40-grid minimum is 0.000 at (160,280) and the 80-grid minimum is 0.044 at (80,400); neither is 0.554, so no stride explains the published number. The mechanism is the pale-window filter: my unfiltered 80x80 pale scan of that still finds 850 windows against the file's 285, a three-fold gap seen on no other still (elsewhere I am within 5 per cent), and the perfectly flat window at (160,280) is cool - R minus B is -6 - so a warmth test excludes it.
corrections.verdict: The shared conclusion of material_truth and anti_goal is right and important: flat.json's prose exempts the sky on numbers - 'the sky's flattest window reads 0.619, which is above 0.363' - that appear nowhere in its own data, whose floor is 0.461 and whose row for that file says 0.554. anti_goal's '61 windows under 0.5' reproduces to the window on the 40-grid. material_truth's diagnosis of why is wrong and would send a fix at the wrong thing.

corrections.claim: The deckle on the voice card at x994-1389 y2554-2733 is two tear masks butted along a straight vertical line at mid-width: 'the top edge steps 21 px at x=1190 (2549 to 2570) with no other jump over 8 px anywhere along its 396 columns'.
corrections.what_i_measured: The join is real and unmistakable: cropping x1090-1300, y2520-2600 at 400 per cent shows a dead-straight vertical cut with a ~21 px step, a shallow fibreless deckle on the left and dense hair strokes on the right; the top edge's largest jump is 21 px at x=1191 and the bottom edge breaks 16 px at the same column, and the left half's top-edge rms is 1.98 px against the right half's 3.84. But 'no other jump over 8 px' is wrong: the top edge has five jumps above 8 px (11 px at x=1304, 10 px at x=1279, x=1313 and x=1237), and the bottom edge has five, including an 18 px jump at x=1141 that is larger than the 16 px break at the claimed join and fifty pixels away from it.
corrections.verdict: Finding confirmed - it is the clearest single anti-goal breach in the set and the crop settles it. The uniqueness argument inside it is overstated and should be dropped; the fibre-density asymmetry, which does reproduce, is the stronger half of the evidence.

corrections.claim: Frames 76-117 'escape the held verdict only because the busiest tile reads 2.2 to 3.0 against a 2.0 floor', their mean and share being 'both far under the 0.5 and 0.0015 thresholds'; the run is '42 frames at step_ms 32 = 1.34 s'.

corrections.what_i_measured: The captured file reads later_check.checked_at = 2026-09-10T17:30:36.137280Z. corrections.claim: The alternate runs show 'the same fling costs 2.47 s and 2.38 s of build for the same 4.80 s of app time (0.5x real time), with zero frames over 400 ms and a worst frame of 77 ms and 76 ms'.
corrections.what_i_measured: True of the fling window and of nothing else. Over the last 300 frames, scroll_webkit_alternates gives 2.47 s / 0 over 400 ms / worst 77 ms and scroll_webkit_plain 2.38 s / 0 / 76 ms - and that window is the file's own ('the_fling_alone: frames 300'), so the comparison with the clip run's last 300 is fair. The critic also lists the two values in the reverse order of the two files it names. Both arms of what_the_alternates_cost.json record 0 heavy frames in the fling, which means the alternates flag the file was built to test is not what distinguishes the fast runs from the slow one - another reason the cause is still unidentified.

The briefing explicitly invites a critic to disagree with the number and say where; one did, on 15_authored_feeling, without reading the field. Nobody checked whether the frame each clip declares as its nearest miss is in fact its quietest. On 15_authored_feeling I found exactly one frame (75) passing all three terms, consistent with repeated_at [74], so the record holds there - but it holds unchecked for the other four clips.

gaps.gap: reliability.json's draft_survival - 'draft and pairing intact after the client process was closed and reopened' - is cited by nobody.
gaps.why_it_matters: 'No lost drafts' is one of the clauses the messenger row names, and it is the review's one omission in the build's favour: the only evidence answering that clause went unread while the critic filed the ordering clause from the same file.

gaps.gap: coldstart.json's host_listener was never cross-read against the code critic's rule 7.
gaps.why_it_matters: Rule 7 is 'the host binds only its tailnet address', scored PARTIAL from the code. coldstart.json - the only recorded run over the real transport - records host_listener '127.0.0.1:8443' with host_reachable_at '100.68.254.25', which is the userspace branch at tailscale_transport.dart:76 (boundTo = isUserspace ? '127.0.0.1' : address). So the clause the code critic could only check statically was not exercised in the one run that could have exercised it; and the port it chose, 8443, is a third voice in the same certificate story the code critic's blocking finding is about.

gaps.gap: No capability check on the second lighting condition beyond the paper.
gaps.why_it_matters: crops/dusk_pulse.png and logs/dusk_pulse.report.json were opened by four readers, but every use of them is a material or anti-goal reading. Nobody asked the messenger or coherence question of the dusk frame - whether a delivery mark, a read mark or the standing line stays legible at the second light - and dusk_pulse.report.json's standing line is one of the seventeen reading '7 hours ago'.

gaps.gap: A looseness in the coherence judgements rule that nobody could have caught but is worth recording.
gaps.why_it_matters: The briefing forbids calling an artifact 'improved' when SSIM says nothing moved. coherence complies, but calls 07_feeling_landing.mp4 'regressed' at SSIM 0.9953 while writing 'almost nothing changed' - the mirror image of the forbidden move, and permitted only because the rule names one direction. All seventeen artifacts are judged and the five 'unchanged' labels are judged 'unchanged', so the report is compliant; the rule is the thing with the hole in it.

verdict: This is a sound review and a markedly more honest one than its own evidence suggests the last was: all six reports carry a real opened list and a reasoned not_worth_opening list, all six fail their floors and all six name exactly one blocking finding, so the arithmetic and the vocabulary agree. Every artifact was opened by four or five readers and every file the last completeness pass named as unread was read this time. I re-measured all six blocking findings and all eighteen serious ones, plus nine minors, and every blocking finding survives: the flat #F1ECDF slabs in 04_moments, the absent haptic evidence, the unlabelled straight-edged arrival card, the beige-with-a-paper-hole voice cards, the certificate story the transport does not implement, and the 49.5 seconds of build time behind 4.80 seconds of scroll. Eleven claims needed correcting. Three matter. The largest is that the two critics who filed the same blocking fault on 04_moments.png disagree by 46 per cent on its size - material_truth's 179,258 px and 3.99 per cent of the frame do not reproduce at all, anti_goal's 260,907 px and 5.81 per cent reproduce to the pixel, and my own count of exact #F1ECDF is 265,995. The second is that emotional_transmission's serious finding that the substitute motion 'stops dead' is wrong: the board does snap in one frame, but the following thirty frames carry 0.13 to 2.08 grey levels of whole-frame change, up to sixty times what the report states and above the brief's own held-frame threshold, and ninety-four per cent of it is the feeling object - the settle the finding says is missing is there, in a different place. The third is that anti_goal's minor on the three 'on the glass' record keys should be withdrawn outright: they are not in the two files it names, they live in the report files, and in 13_messenger_states.report.json all three are populated with exactly the refusal string the critic says the record fails to carry. Two further corrections run the other way and strengthen the build's critics rather than weakening them - no still in the set casts a contact shadow on any side by my measurement, where material_truth credited three of them with one, and all ten stills have a median free edge under 1.0 px rms, not nine under 1.30. What the review as a whole did not do is look past the numbers to the causes: the single figure holding the heaviest row at its floor was read by one critic, the cause named inside that finding is unmeasurable from anything in the set, and the cause the evidence offers for itself - 276 ms a row - is falsified by a two-column join of two files already in the set. Alongside that sit three records this cycle was told to write and nobody opened: load.made_of, the three per-clip .frames.json files for the very clips the blocking findings turn on, and lines.json's self-declared failure at 0.341, which is the one published fault in the whole capture that no report scored.
